overall: Atlanta reached a running max of 93.2°F around 13:55 ET, then experienced a sharp afternoon drop to the mid-80s around 14:52—consistent with thunderstorm outflow or a convective pulse—before partially recovering to 91.4°F by 15:52. Conditions are running cooler than the NWS text forecast of 95°F suggests, and an active Severe Thunderstorm Warning (until 4:15 PM EDT near Trion/Summerville, moving east) signals ongoing convective disruption that is likely capping further afternoon heating.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is notably spread: GFS at 97.4°F is a clear warm outlier against ECMWF (91.5°F), HRRR (94.2°F), and NBM (92.9°F), with the fused META model splitting probability mass between 94-95F and 96-97F buckets. max_temp_prediction: The daily high is most likely already in the books at 93.2°F, placing today squarely in the 93-94°F odd bucket (the active Kalshi market's top probability bucket at 36.3%). While the partial temperature recovery to 91.4°F by 15:52 leaves a slim window for a marginal new max if skies briefly clear before additional convective activity arrives, the severe thunderstorm warning and give-up classifier fire make any meaningful exceedance of 93.2°F unlikely. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the final TMAX will land between 93.0°F and 94.0°F.
